overview: File covers Admiral Hasegawa's 1940 appointment as Taiwan's Governor-General, read by US observers as tying the post to Japan's southward naval strategy rather than routine colonial administration.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to Hornbeck on Japanese naval commanders at Shanghai
subfiles.about: The memorandum answers a question about which Japanese admirals commanded or directed naval landing forces at Shanghai in 1932 and later commanded there in 1937–38.
subfiles.summary: Memo identifies Hasegawa and other Japanese naval commanders active at Shanghai in 1932 and 1937-38.

subfiles.title: Fragmentary inquiry concerning a commander in 1932
subfiles.about: A brief internal question, preserved in severely garbled OCR, appears to concern the identity or position of a chief or commander associated with events in 1932.
subfiles.summary: Fragmentary note likely records an inquiry about a 1932 Japanese naval commander, now largely illegible.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Grew on Hasegawa’s appointment as Governor-General of Formosa
subfiles.about: Grew reports Hasegawa’s appointment as Governor-General of Formosa and the belief that it signaled greater emphasis on Japan’s southward advance.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Admiral Hasegawa's appointment as Taiwan's Governor-General, staying on active duty, seen as tied to southward expansion.

subfiles.title: Naval attaché report on the strategic meaning of Hasegawa’s appointment
subfiles.to: Office of the Chief of Naval Operations; information to the Assistant U.S. Naval Attaché, Shanghai, and Commander in Chief, Asiatic Fleet
subfiles.about: The naval attaché argues that Hasegawa’s appointment was intended to coordinate naval expansion into the South Seas rather than to provide routine colonial administration.
subfiles.summary: Naval attaché reads Hasegawa's active-duty governorship as growing naval influence, hinting Taiwan and South Seas administration may merge.

interest: Shows Japan's 1940 choice of a sitting admiral to govern Taiwan, read as signaling southward military expansion.
